articles.name: Setting up the end-user experience for messaging
articles.title: Setting up the end-user experience for messaging
articles.body:
When you migrate to messaging, your end users are migrating as well. Take time to plan how you want customers to experience messaging.

When you migrate to messaging, your end users are migrating as well. Take time to plan how you want customers to experience messaging.

You are likely using live chat configuration options that have equivalent options in messaging. There are also options in messaging that are unavailable in Chat.

Use this article as a high-level walkthrough of the main customer-facing settings to review during migration.
Note: If you went through the assisted migration experience, some of the options described below may have already been migrated to Admin Center.

This article includes the following topics:

  • Step 1: Setting up your messaging channel
  • Step 2: Configuring greetings and customer data capture
  • Step 3: Showing wait time and queue updates
  • Step 4: Planning for outside of business hours
  • Step 5: Configuring CSAT
  • Additional considerations

Related articles:

  • Overview of the migration workflow
  • Configuring messaging responses and business hours
  • Viewing and configuring Web Widget settings

Comparing live chat and messaging end-user experience options

The following table maps common Chat configuration options to their equivalents in messaging settings.

Live chat configuration Messaging configuration
Pre-chat form

AI agent or

Collecting customer details in the basic messaging response
Offline form or web form for outside of business hours Migrating Chat operating hours to business hours in messaging
Branding on SDKs Viewing and configuring Web Widget settings
Queue position Estimated wait time and queue position
Proactive messaging using Chat triggers Proactive messaging
Authentication Setting up authentication for messaging
Web or Mobile SDKs API reference for web and mobile SDK
Chat Conversation APIs SunCo Switchboard APIs

Step 1: Setting up your messaging channel

After you’ve migrated your account from Chat to messaging, you’ll need to set up your Web Widget or mobile SDK channel. You can configure the channel settings that affect the customer experience, such as branding, responses, wait time, authentication, and installation.

Set up and manage these settings for both Web Widget and mobile SDK channels on the Messaging settings page in Admin Center:

  • Brands connected to your messaging channels
  • Advanced settings:
    • Downloading transcripts, to allow end users to download conversation transcripts
    • Multi-conversations, to allow customers to conduct multiple messaging conversations
    • Capacity release, to define how agent capacity is managed and conversation reminders are sent
    • Ending sessions, to allow users to end messaging sessions
    • Email identities, to allow end users to use email addresses to identify themselves
    • Conversation control, to manage how conversations are handled when resolved
    • AI agent conversations as tickets in Agent Workspace, to allow human agents to see conversations between end users and AI agents in Agent Workspace

Note: If you used the migration wizard to initiate your move to messaging, an embeddable Web Widget or mobile SDK channel appears in the Messaging channels list.

Configure these Web Widget settings by clicking the name of the Web Widget on the Channels page in Admin Center:

  • Basics: Web Widget name, channel linking, and privacy notice
  • Style: Web Widget appearance, including colors, logo, widget position, attachment permissions, launcher shape, and text
  • Responses: Default messaging responses for customers. See Step 2.
  • Wait time: Display how long end users may wait for agent assistance
  • Authentication: Security settings for authenticated and unauthenticated visitors
  • Installation: Code snippet and help center embed

Configure these mobile channel settings by clicking the name of the mobile channel on the Channels page in Admin Center:

  • Basics: Channel name
  • Style: Channel appearance, including colors, title, and description
  • Responses: Business hours, default messaging response, and AI agent activation. See Step 2.
  • Notifications: Push notification settings
  • Authentication: Security settings for authenticated and unauthenticated users
  • Installation: Channel ID and help center embed

For more information, see:

  • Viewing and configuring Web Widget settings
  • Configuring mobile channel settings

Step 2: Configuring greetings and customer data capture

Your customers’ first interaction with your messaging channel is defined in the Responses settings for the Web Widget or mobile channel.

Use these settings to greet customers, set expectations, and collect basic information before an agent joins the conversation.

You can also use messaging triggers to send queue-related messages, such as:

  • A confirmation that the request was received
  • An update when the customer is assigned to an agent

Similarly, if you use AI agents, you can also capture customer details such as name and email before the conversation is handed off.

For more information, see:

  • Configuring messaging responses and business hours
  • Customizing the standard responses for an AI agent for messaging

Step 3: Showing wait time and queue updates

Estimated wait time and queue position can help customers understand when they can expect agent assistance. This can improve the messaging experience, especially during busy periods.

If you use Sunshine Conversations SDKs, you can also send wait time updates with messaging triggers.

For more information, see:

  • Displaying wait time estimates in messaging conversations

Step 4: Planning for outside of business hours

Decide how messaging should behave when customers contact you outside of business hours. For example, you can send an automatic response, collect customer information, or direct customers to self-service resources.

For more information, see:

  • Migrating Chat operating hours to business hours in messaging
  • Configuring messaging responses and business hours

Step 5: Configuring CSAT

Messaging supports a more flexible CSAT experience than Chat. You can choose when to send the survey and align it with your messaging workflow.

In most cases, it’s best to send CSAT when the ticket is resolved.

For more information, see:

  • About the CSAT user experience for email and messaging
  • Sending a CSAT survey to your customers

Additional considerations

Depending on your current Chat setup, you may also need to review:

  • Proactive messaging
  • Setting up user authentication for messaging
  • Voice messaging SDK documentation

articles.name: Migrating Chat operating hours to business hours in messaging
articles.title: Migrating Chat operating hours to business hours in messaging
articles.body:
If you use operating hours in your Zendesk Chat configuration, you’ll likely want to apply a similar schedule to your messaging configuration.

If you use operating hours in your Zendesk Chat configuration, you’ll likely want to apply a similar schedule to your messaging configuration.

This article provides an overview of how business hours work on messaging, how they differ from Chat operating hours, and common workflows you can use to manage conversations outside business hours.

This article includes the following topics:

  • About messaging business hours
  • Managing the end user’s experience and expectations
  • Workflows to handle offline messaging tickets

Related articles:

  • About AI agents
  • Configuring messaging responses and business hours
  • Setting your schedule with business hours and holidays

About messaging business hours

In Zendesk Chat, operating hours mainly control when chat is available. Unlike Chat, messaging can function asynchronously. In messaging, business hours and schedules can control several different behaviors.

For example, in messaging, business hours and schedules can control:

  • Whether customers can start a conversation
  • Whether an AI agent can escalate to a human agent
  • Whether a ticket is created outside business hours
  • What message customers see when agents are unavailable

Because of this, there isn’t a one-to-one replacement for Chat operating hours in messaging. Instead, choose the messaging setup that best matches the experience you want to provide.

Use the following table to map common Chat operating hours use cases to messaging options:

If you used Chat operating hours to… In messaging, use…
Let customers know agents are offline Triggers to deliver automated responses outside of business hours
Offer self-service after hours AI agents with schedules
Let customers leave a request for follow-up AI agent tickets
Route after-hours requests differently Triggers and routing workflows

Managing the end user’s experience and expectations

When migrating from Chat to messaging, decide what you want customers to experience outside business hours. You can configure your messaging channel to do one of the following:

  • Option 1: Offer self-service with an AI agent
  • Option 2: Hide the widget outside business hours
  • Option 3: Prevent escalation to an agent outside business hours
  • Option 4: Let customers create a ticket for follow-up

Option 1: Offer self-service with an AI agent (recommended)

Agentic AI agents are available 24/7 to provide support when your human agents are unavailable. An AI agent can respond to support requests through your messaging channel, perform tasks, and offer assistance that can resolve customer issues without input from a human agent.

If you use schedules, you can create an AI agent that behaves differently based on the day or time of day when your customer submits their support request.

Step 1: Create your schedule in Admin Center

You can create a regular weekly schedule and a holiday schedule in Admin Center as needed.
Note: If you're using the assisted migration experience, your Chat schedules will be automatically migrated to Admin Center.

Step 2: Create and configure an agentic AI agent for your messaging channel

  1. Create your AI agent for messaging, making sure to select the brand with a comprehensive knowledge base.
  2. In the AI agents workspace, select the newly-created AI agent.
  3. If your help center is able to provide the AI agent with a useful response, the conversation can end there; however, if the agent is unable to provide the customer with a resolution, make sure you customize the AI agent's Escalation reply with a message that is sent outside of business hours.

Step 3: Test and publish the AI agent

  1. Test the AI agent to confirm it performs as expected.
  2. Activate the AI agent on your messaging channel.

Option 2: Hide the widget outside business hours

You can choose to hide the Web Widget when agents aren’t available using the Core messaging Javascript API.

This option is best for accounts that:

  • Aren't using AI agents or a messaging configuration for customers to self-solve their issues, so deflection isn’t available.
  • Don't have a help center or other knowledge source from which an automated answer, through an AI agent or messaging response, can be generated.
  • Only have potential resolutions that require input from human agents.

Option 3: Prevent escalation to an agent outside business hours

If you have a robust help center or external knowledge source, you can rely on an AI agent or messaging response to offer customers the opportunity to resolve common issues without input from a human agent, and prevent them from submitting a ticket when human agents aren’t available.

Step 1: Create your schedule in Admin Center

You can create a regular weekly schedule and a holiday schedule in Admin Center as needed.

Step 2: Create your automated responder

You can use an AI agent, or a standard messaging response if you aren’t using AI agents, to communicate with your customers outside of your business hours.

For an AI agent

  1. Create the AI agent for your messaging channel.
  2. Customize the fallback reply by selecting the schedule you created that sets your business hours. For the Outside business hours part of the reply, deselect Add option to talk to a human and escalate. This prevents a ticket from being created when the AI agent escalates the conversation. Fill out the message you want your customers to receive, including any instructions for contacting agents through other channels or ways to self-solve their issue.

For the Web Widget or mobile SDK, without AI agents

  1. Create or edit your Web Widget or mobile SDK messaging channel.
  2. Configure the messaging response.
    • Select the schedule you created that sets your business hours.
    • Click Outside business hours, then fill out the message you want your customers to receive, including any instructions for contacting agents through other channels or ways to self-solve their issue.

Workflows to handle offline messaging tickets

In addition to the options above, you can create triggers to make sure the workflow for support requests submitted outside of business hours are handled correctly.

This section includes the following options:

  • Workflow 1: Route offline conversations to a specific group
  • Workflow 2: Assign offline tickets with lower priority
  • Workflow 3: Re-route offline conversations to follow up over email

Workflow 1: Route offline conversations to a specific group

The following ticket trigger sends new conversations that come in after hours to a specific group, in this case one that manages tickets that come in outside of business hours.

Step 1: Ensure your account has the required elements
  • Create a group in Support for handling these tickets, for example Overnight requests
  • Define business hours for basic messaging users, or create a schedule for AI agent users
Step 2: Create the ticket trigger

Create a ticket trigger using the following conditions and actions:

Meet ALL of the following conditions:

  • Ticket > Status category | Is | New
  • Ticket > Within business hours? | Is | No

Actions:

  • Ticket > Add tags | offline_conversations
  • Ticket > Messaging session | End Session
  • Ticket > Group | Overnight requests group

Workflow 2: Assign offline tickets with lower priority

This option creates offline messaging tickets that are handled by the same team responding to messaging tickets that come in after hours, but with lower priority. This option is only possible with omnichannel routing, which allows the queue to be ordered based on ticket priority.

Step 1: Ensure your account has the required elements
  • Omnichannel routing is turned on
  • Messaging activity routing is turned on. This keeps all tickets, both active and inactive, in the team or agent queue, including offline tickets.
  • Define business hours for basic messaging users, or create a schedule for AI agent users
Step 2: Create the ticket trigger

Create a ticket trigger that assigns a lower priority to tickets created outside of business hours, using the following conditions and actions:

Meet ALL of the following conditions:

  • Ticket > Channel | Is | Messaging
  • Ticket > Within business hours? | Is | No

Actions:

  • Ticket > Priority | Low

Workflow 3: Re-route offline conversations to follow up over email

Create a ticket trigger to re-route offline conversations.

  • Event: When ticket is Created
  • Conditions:
    • Status is New
    • Ticket > Within business hours | No
  • Actions:
    • Ticket tag | offline_conversations
    • Set messaging session state = Ended
    • Group = Email group

articles.name: Choosing and implementing your conversational style
articles.title: Choosing and implementing your conversational style
articles.body:
With messaging, you can choose the conversational style that best fits your business and customer experience. A conversational style determines how long messaging conversations stay open and how customers continue an existing conversation.

With messaging, you can choose the conversational style that best fits your business and customer experience. A conversational style determines how long messaging conversations stay open and how customers continue an existing conversation.

Use this article to compare the available conversational styles and understand the high-level workflow for implementing each one. For detailed setup instructions, follow the linked configuration articles.

This article covers the following topics:

  • Comparing conversational styles
  • Choosing the right style for your workflow

Related articles:

  • Conversational styles in messaging
  • Configuring the live chat conversational style
  • Configuring the live chat conversational style for returning customers

Comparing conversational styles

Conversational style Best option for Basic workflow
Live chat

Single set of synchronous live interactions with a clear start

 Transactional businesses, simple support issues, organizations using the Web Widget as their primary conversational channel, and teams migrating from Chat. Create a Support ticket trigger that closes messaging tickets soon after they’re solved. See Configuring the live chat conversational style.
Returning customer/reopened conversations

Multiple sets of live interactions

 Businesses whose customers often return within a short period of time to continue the same conversation, and teams that want a short reopen window after a conversation is solved. Create a Support automation that closes solved messaging tickets after a short delay, such as one hour. See Configuring the live chat conversational style for returning customers.
Social messaging/asynchronous conversations

Multiple live and non-live interactions

 Less transactional businesses, complex issues that take longer to resolve, and workflows that require coordination with other teams or third parties. Use the standard Support automation that closes solved tickets after several days, or adjust the timing to fit your workflow. See About the standard Support automations and Creating and managing automations for time-based events.

Choosing the right style for your workflow

Choose a conversational style based on how your customers typically interact with your business and how long you want conversations to remain open.

Use the following guidance:

  • Choose the live chat conversational style if your support interactions are short, transactional, and usually resolved in a single session.
  • Choose the returning customer conversational style if customers often come back shortly after a conversation is solved and need to continue discussing the same issue.
  • Choose the social messaging conversational style if conversations often continue over a longer period of time or require follow-up across teams.

If you're migrating from Chat, the live chat conversational style or returning customer conversational style is often the best starting point.

articles.name: Migrating from Chat routing to omnichannel routing
articles.title: Migrating from Chat routing to omnichannel routing
articles.body:
One of the main benefits of moving to messaging is access toomnichannel routing. Omnichannel routing is a routing engine that automatically assigns tickets from any channel to the best available agent using a consistent approach.

One of the main benefits of moving to messaging is access to omnichannel routing. Omnichannel routing is a routing engine that automatically assigns tickets from any channel to the best available agent using a consistent approach.

Omnichannel routing is the default routing engine for all new Zendesk accounts. With a single routing configuration, you can control:

  • Prioritization
  • Assignment
  • Skills-based routing
  • Reassignment
  • Agent acceptance

You can continue using your existing group structure, or move to custom queues for more advanced routing scenarios. For example, custom queues can help with routing to multiple groups, overflow handling, and percentage-based routing.

Some capabilities depend on your plan. For more information, see About omnichannel routing.

This article includes the following topics:

  • Key concepts
  • Setting up omnichannel routing

Before setting up omnichannel routing, it’s recommended that you understand some key concepts.

Key concepts

The following list includes high-level descriptions of key messaging and omnichannel routing terminology and concepts. Use the links in each list item to learn more.

  • Capacity: The maximum number of Open tickets that can be assigned to an agent. Capacity rules, omnichannel routing’s equivalent of Chat limits, are used to define the maximum capacity of an agent for each channel. Capacity is released when an agent marks the ticket as Pending, On-hold, or Solved, or when a conversation becomes inactive. See Managing end user presence and automatic capacity release.
  • Conversation: For the messaging channel, this equates to the entire lifecycle of a customer request. A conversation begins when the end user enters their first comment in the Web Widget, mobile SDK, or social messaging channel, and ends when the related ticket status is Closed.
  • Session: For the messaging channel, the real-time live chat-style interaction between an end user and a human or AI agent. The session can be ended by the ticket being Closed, ended manually by an end user or the agent, or automatically using a business rule that includes the End session action. Once the session has ended, the end user is prevented from interacting any further with that conversation, and the agent can continue to work on the associated ticket.
  • Skills: Skills are attributes that are applied to the ticket and given to agents that provide more granular control over which tickets are routed to which agents. Skills for omnichannel routing span all channels. Typical skills include languages, product expertise, and permission to handle VIP requests. Omnichannel routing can use skills to further refine your ticket routing. See About using skills to route tickets for more details.
  • State: The activity status of a messaging session can be one of these three states:
    • Active if an end user has responded to the ticket within the allowed idle period. By default, this is set to 10 minutes.
    • Inactive if the end user has not responded within the allowed idle period, or if the ticket status is set to Pending, On-hold, or Solved. An inactive session can become active if the end user responds.
    • Ended is a terminal state. Ended sessions can’t be reactivated. Agents and end users can’t communicate in an ended session.
  • Unified agent status: The way an agent controls their availability in omnichannel routing. This replaces individual channel statuses, which only allowed an agent to control their availability for one channel at a time.

Setting up omnichannel routing

This section provides a high-level guide to moving from Chat-based routing to omnichannel routing, and some key differences between Chat and omnichannel routing settings and elements.

This section includes the following steps:

  • Step 1: Prepare to migrate to omnichannel routing
  • Step 2: Record your Chat routing settings
  • Step 3: Recreate your chat limits as omnichannel capacity rules
  • Step 4: Recreate chat skills as agent skills
  • Step 5: Configure additional omnichannel routing settings
  • Step 6: Convert Automatic Idle time to omnichannel idle timeout
  • Step 7: Turn on omnichannel routing

Note: If you’ve gone through the voluntary live-chat-to-messaging migration process, your routing is still determined by your Chat settings. Follow the steps below to migrate to omnichannel routing.

Step 1: Prepare to migrate to omnichannel routing

The tasks below can help ensure the migration to omnichannel routing goes smoothly.

  • Review your current routing strategy across your Zendesk environment, including Chat, email, social messaging, and Zendesk Voice. Consider:
    • How your Support team is organized
    • Whether you use skills to route tickets to agents
    • How tickets are grouped
    • How chat limits are determined
    • How tickets are prioritized
    • How ticket reassignment is handled
  • Plan your future routing strategy by reviewing the omnichannel routing documentation and planning for your current and future routing needs. Omnichannel routing applies across your entire account and includes several improvements over live chat, such as:
    • Built-in prioritization by ticket priority or SLA
    • An omnichannel approach to capacity
    • An omnichannel routing queue or custom queues
    • A unified agent status
    • Auto-acceptance of tickets
    • Real-time monitoring
    • Integration with intelligent triage
  • Prepare your agents for the upcoming changes. Let them know when and why you’re migrating. Give them access to the information they need, and make sure they know the basics of working with omnichannel routing.

Step 2: Record your Chat routing settings

Before you activate omnichannel routing, record your Chat routing settings where you can access them later. They won’t be visible after omnichannel routing is turned on, but you’ll want to reference them in subsequent steps.

Step 3: Recreate your chat limits as omnichannel capacity rules

Chat dashboard setting Admin Center setting
Settings > Routing > Settings tab > Chat limit Objects and rules > Omnichannel routing > Capacity rules

Capacity rules are the messaging equivalent of chat limits.

Both allow you to cap the number of incoming chat notifications assigned or broadcast to each agent. Capacity rules offer a more nuanced approach to ticket assignment – for example, Chat limits look at the number of currently-active tickets assigned to agents, while capacity rules let you choose whether to include inactive tickets towards an agent's limit, and automatically adjusts their capacity as ticket activity status changes. For more information about how capacity rules work, and instructions for configuring them, see Creating capacity rules to balance agent workloads.

Step 4: Recreate chat skills as agent skills

Chat dashboard setting Admin Center setting
Settings > Routing > Skills tab Objects and rules > Business rules > Skills

If you use Chat skills, or want to use skills in your omnichannel routing configuration, you’ll need to create them as agent skills in Admin Center, assign these skills to agents, and create triggers to apply the skills to tickets.

Step 5: Configure additional omnichannel routing settings

Chat dashboard setting Admin Center setting
Settings > Routing Objects and rules > Omnichannel routing > Routing configuration

Follow the guidelines in managing your omnichannel routing configuration to configure how your routing engine will work.

The following table describes some of the differences in how live chat and omnichannel routing manage key routing settings and define important concepts.

Setting In Chat In omnichannel routing
Ticket sorting All tickets are ordered by time of arrival. All tickets are ordered by time of arrival unless you are on Professional or Enterprise plans, where the default is by ticket priority and then time of arrival. For example, Urgent oldest ticket first. You can also choose to order tickets by Next SLA Breach.
Assignment method Can be either Broadcast, which notifies all agents of an incoming request, or Assigned, which notifies only a specific agent of an incoming request. Only supports Assigned mode, which is more efficient than Broadcast mode. It can also use highest spare capacity, highest spare capacity by percentage, and round robin to distribute tickets to agents.
Skills-based routing Uses Chat skills to route tickets to the appropriate agents. Uses skills shared across all channels to route tickets to appropriate agents.
Focus mode Prevents an agent active on a Chat, or a Voice call, from being assigned tickets on the other real-time channel. Prevents an agent active on messaging, or a Voice call, from being assigned tickets on the other real-time channel.
Reassignment In assigned mode, you can control how long to wait for an agent to accept the incoming Chat before attempting to reassign it to another agent. Messaging reassignment timing allows you to configure how long to wait for an agent to accept the incoming messaging ticket before attempting to reassign it to another agent. Other advanced options include reassignment of reopened tickets to another agent, auto-assignment of Open tickets to another agent when an agent changes their status, and reassignment through queues to reevaluate a reassigned ticket against custom queue conditions.

Step 6: Convert Automatic Idle time to omnichannel idle timeout

Chat dashboard setting Admin Center setting
Settings > Personal > Idle timeout tab Objects and rules > Omnichannel routing > Status timeout

In Chat, agents can set an automatic idle time after which their status can be updated from Online to Away or Invisible. Omnichannel routing’s idle timeout setting allows admins to set the idle time and disconnection behavior for each agent status.

Step 7: Turn on omnichannel routing

You’re now ready to turn on and configure omnichannel routing.

To turn on omnichannel routing

  1. In Admin Center, go to Objects and rules > Routing configuration.
  2. Click Turn on omnichannel routing.

    When you turn on omnichannel routing:

    • Chat routing functionality is turned off and all Chat routing settings in the Chat dashboard are hidden.
    • Changes to agent status and Explore reporting are applied. See Considerations for using omnichannel routing with Chat.

articles.name: Migrating from Chat analytics to messaging reporting
articles.title: Migrating from Chat analytics to messaging reporting
articles.body:
When you migrate from Chat to messaging, you can use real-time monitoring dashboards, the Explore Messaging dashboard, or both to monitor ticket volume, agent activity, and customer experience. There’s no automated way to migrate your Chat analytics setup, so you need to recreate your reporting manually in the messaging tools you plan to use. This article explains the available reporting options, how to prepare for the transition, and how common Chat analytics metrics map to messaging reporting.

When you migrate from Chat to messaging, you can use real-time monitoring dashboards, the Explore Messaging dashboard, or both to monitor ticket volume, agent activity, and customer experience. There’s no automated way to migrate your Chat analytics setup, so you need to recreate your reporting manually in the messaging tools you plan to use. This article explains the available reporting options, how to prepare for the transition, and how common Chat analytics metrics map to messaging reporting.

This article includes the following topics:

  • About the messaging reporting options
  • Preparing to migrate
  • Setting up real-time monitoring
  • Setting up the Explore Messaging dashboard
  • Comparing Chat analytics and messaging reporting
  • Understanding common reporting changes after migration

For more information on messaging reporting and analysis, see the following articles:

  • About real-time monitoring dashboards
  • Accessing the real-time monitoring dashboards
  • Overview of the Zendesk Messaging dashboard
  • Analyzing your messaging tickets
  • Metrics and attributes for Zendesk messaging

About the messaging reporting options

You can use one or both of Zendesk's reporting options for messaging:

  • Real-time monitoring dashboards, which provide live, operational, omnichannel visibility and recent historical data for up to 30 days.
  • The Explore Messaging dashboard, which provides historical reporting for messaging tickets and performance trends. It doesn’t include live performance data.

These options offer different views into how, and how well, your messaging configuration is working, and you can use them in tandem. Use real-time monitoring to manage current and recent workload and agent activity. Use the Explore Messaging dashboard to analyze historical performance and trends.

Real-time monitoring

Real-time monitoring:

  • Organizes reporting by workflow instead of by channel, which can make it easier to monitor day-to-day support operations.
  • Shows live data that helps you make immediate staffing and queue management decisions.
  • Includes recent historical data for many reports, so you can review trends over the past 30 days.

By default, real-time monitoring includes these dashboards:

  • Incoming tickets (requires omnichannel routing)
  • Ticket progress
  • Agent productivity

For more information, see About real-time monitoring dashboards.

The Explore Messaging dashboard

The Explore Messaging dashboard:

  • Provides historical reporting for messaging tickets and agent performance.
  • Includes reports for metrics such as first reply time, agent activity, and messaging goal conversions.
  • Shows historical data from the date Explore was enabled for the account, as far back as August 2021.

For more information, see Overview of the Zendesk Messaging dashboard.

Preparing to migrate

Currently, reporting settings from Chat analytics are not included as part of the automated migration tool. You need to recreate your reporting setup manually in real-time monitoring and the Explore Messaging dashboard.

To prepare for the transition from Chat analytics to messaging reporting

  • Review the reports you use today. Identify which reports are still useful, which metrics matter most, and which dashboards you don’t need to recreate.
  • Learn how messaging reporting differs from Chat analytics. Review the metric comparison section in this article. Some Chat metrics don’t have direct messaging equivalents, so you may need to adjust how you measure performance.
  • Review the available reporting tools. Familiarize yourself with real-time monitoring and the Explore Messaging dashboard, including the filters, dashboards, and reports available in each.
  • Make a reporting plan. List the queues, teams, filters, and key metrics you want to monitor in each tool.
  • Review how messaging changes performance metrics. See Metrics that matter: Measuring success when migrating from live chat to messaging to understand how messaging workflows can affect the way you evaluate team performance.

Setting up real-time monitoring

Use real-time monitoring if you need live visibility into queue backlog, in-progress work, and agent activity.

To set up real-time monitoring

  1. Access the real-time monitoring dashboards. See Accessing the real-time monitoring dashboards.
  2. Review the available dashboards:
    • Incoming tickets
    • Ticket progress
    • Agent productivity
  3. If you want to use the full set of real-time messaging dashboards, make sure omnichannel routing is configured where required.
  4. Apply filters and drill into the dashboards to focus on the brands, groups, channels, and agents you want to monitor.

You can’t create custom reports in real-time monitoring. However, you can use filters and drill-ins to review ticket and agent activity in more detail.

Setting up the Explore Messaging dashboard

Use the Explore Messaging dashboard if you need historical reporting for messaging performance and trends.

To set up the Explore Messaging dashboard

  1. Open the Zendesk Messaging dashboard in Explore.
  2. Review the prebuilt reports available in the dashboard.
  3. Identify the reports that match the metrics you tracked in Chat analytics.
  4. If needed, create custom reports in Explore to support your reporting requirements.
  5. Validate your filters, date ranges, and datasets so your reports reflect the messaging activity you want to measure.

For more information, see Analyzing your messaging tickets.

Comparing Chat analytics and messaging reporting

Many Chat analytics metrics have equivalent or near-equivalent metrics in messaging reporting. In some cases, there isn’t a direct match because messaging workflows differ from chat workflows.

Use the following tables to identify where common Chat analytics metrics appear in real-time monitoring or the Explore Messaging dashboard.

Monitoring data

Chat metric Real-time monitoring Explore messaging reporting Notes
Chat Analytics or Chat engagements dataset N/A Messaging dataset and Messaging engagement dataset Messaging reporting may require a different dataset than the one you used for Chat.
Monitor or Live data dashboard in Explore Real-time monitoring dashboards N/A Use real-time monitoring for live operational visibility.
Visitor list for monitoring agents Agent productivity real-time dashboard Agent productivity reporting  
Visitor list for monitoring queues Incoming tickets and In-progress tickets Incoming tickets reporting  

Metrics for ticket volume

Chat metric Real-time monitoring Explore messaging reporting Notes
Chats Active conversations in queue Messaging tickets Messaging tickets count tickets created from messaging channels, not chat sessions
Completed chats Solved tickets Solved tickets  
Missed inbound chats Missed conversations Missed conversations (workflow-dependent)  
Dropped chats N/A No direct equivalent Messaging conversations are persistent, so dropped chats don’t map directly.
Transferred chats Reassigned messaging tickets Reassigned messaging tickets  
Offline messages Messaging tickets created outside of business hours Messaging tickets created outside of business hours  

Metrics for customer experience

Chat metric Real-time monitoring Explore messaging reporting Notes
% Chat satisfaction score Satisfaction (overall) Good satisfaction tickets The calculation method may differ between tools.
Chat duration (sec) Chat duration Full resolution time (min) These metrics are related, but they don’t measure exactly the same behavior.
Chat wait time (sec) Wait time First reply time (sec)  
Chat first reply time (sec) Response time First reply time (sec) In messaging, first reply time doesn’t include bot replies in the same way Chat can.
Chat average reply time (sec) Response time Requester wait time average (sec)  
Chat agent messages N/A Agent messages  
Chat visitor messages N/A Requester messages  
Assignments N/A Assignee stations, Assignee changes, or assignment-related metrics  

Metrics for agent and queue monitoring

Chat metric Real-time monitoring Explore messaging reporting Notes
Chat wait time N/A Assignment to first reply (sec)  
Engagement duration (min) Average and longest handle time Handle time (min)  
% Assignment acceptance rate Agent productivity metrics Acceptance rate  
Time spent online/away/invisible Agent availability views Agent time in state  
Average concurrency Capacity in use Agent average used capacity  

Monitoring queues and agents in real time

If you used Chat Monitor, Live data dashboard, or Visitor List in Chat, the following real-time monitoring dashboards are the closest messaging equivalents:

Chat metric Real-time monitoring equivalent
Queue Incoming tickets
Wait time Incoming tickets and Ticket progress
Response time Ticket progress
Chat duration Ticket progress
Currently served chats Agent productivity
Chats per agent Agent productivity
Drill down into agents Agent productivity
Drill down into queues Incoming tickets

Understanding common reporting changes after migration

After you migrate from Chat to messaging, you may notice changes in reported volume, wait time, first reply time, and handle time. These changes are often caused by differences between chat and messaging workflows rather than by a reporting error.

This section includes the following reporting changes:

  • Increase in first reply time for messaging tickets vs chat tickets
  • Increase in ticket volume after migration
  • Increase in agent handle time

Increase in first reply time for messaging tickets vs chat tickets

Issue: You notice an increase in first reply time after moving to messaging.

Possible causes include:

  • Account uses custom bot in Chat
    • In Chat, first reply time can include the AI agent’s first response.
    • In messaging, first reply time measures the time from handoff to the first human agent reply.
  • Messaging ticket volume has increased
    • More tickets in queue can increase first reply time.
  • Wait time in queue has increased
    • Reopened or unassigned messaging tickets can affect response times.
  • Agent handle time has increased
    • If agents hold capacity longer or tickets are reassigned frequently, first reply time can increase.

For a more accurate comparison, compare Chat engagement-based first reply metrics with messaging assignment-to-first-reply metrics where appropriate.

Recommended actions:

  • Create reports with the following KPIs for messaging and Chat:
    • Messaging ticket volume.
    • First assignment or queue wait time.
    • Reassignment volume.
    • Agent acceptance rate.
    • Agent handle time.

Increase in ticket volume after migration

Issue: You notice more messaging tickets than you previously saw in Chat reporting.

Possible cause: Messaging reporting can include conversations that were handled differently in Chat, including tickets created outside business hours and conversations that remain active across a longer lifecycle.

Recommended actions:

  • Review how your reporting handles:
    • Tickets created outside business hours.
    • Reopened conversations.
    • Workflow-driven conversation handling.
  • Use business-hours-based metrics where appropriate to exclude time spent waiting outside scheduled support hours.
  • Review your routing and workflow configuration if you want messaging behavior to more closely match your previous Chat workflows.

Increase in wait time due to agent capacity

Issue: Agents aren’t releasing capacity quickly enough.

Recommended actions:

  • Turn on automatic capacity release.
  • Adjust the inactivity timeout to match your support workflow.
  • Review whether agents are setting ticket status appropriately when work is complete or waiting on the customer.

Issue: Tickets are being reassigned frequently.

Recommended actions:

  • Review agent acceptance rate.
  • Turn on automatic conversation acceptance if it fits your workflow.
  • Review your skills and capacity rules.

Issue: Reopened messaging tickets are holding agent capacity.

Recommended actions:

  • Turn on omnichannel routing if you haven’t already.
  • Configure omnichannel routing to reassign reopened messaging tickets to available agents.

Increase in resolution time

Issue: Resolution time increases after migration.

Possible causes include:

  • The same ticket stays open longer and is reused for multiple customer interactions.
  • Your account uses a returning-user conversational style, which can extend the lifecycle of a messaging ticket.

Recommended actions:

  • Review your ticket lifecycle and solve workflow.
  • Make sure agents solve tickets when the issue is resolved.
  • Adjust your reporting expectations to account for the longer-lived nature of messaging conversations.

Increase in agent handle time

Issue: Agent handle time increases after migration.

Recommended actions:

  • Review whether agents are releasing capacity promptly.
  • Turn on automatic capacity release.
  • Review whether agents are moving tickets to Pending, On-hold, or Solved when appropriate.

articles.name: Release notes through 2026-07-17
articles.title: Release notes through 2026-07-17
articles.body:
See the What's New section for an overview of what was released last month.

This week's release notes include:

  • Voice
  • Knowledge
  • Copilot
  • AI agents
  • App Marketplace
  • Products with no updates this week

Voice

New:

  •  Agents can now change the incoming call ringtone and adjust the incoming call volume.  For more information. See Receiving incoming calls.

Fixed:

  • When an agent makes an outbound call and the end user declines or blocks the call, the agent will now see an error message informing them the call was declined or busy. Previously, the call would end without any indication or error message.    

Knowledge

New:

  • Contentful is now available as a knowledge source. You can connect Contentful to your Zendesk account to make the content available wherever external content is used.
  • Jira is now available as a knowledge source. You can connect Jira to your Zendesk account to make the content available wherever external content is used.
  • We’ve released an Early Access Program (EAP) for the conversational help center experience, delivered through the new Lisbon theme. This EAP introduces an AI-powered help center layout that combines natural-language question answering with standard help center navigation, allowing end users to ask questions and receive quick answers generated from your published content.

Fixed: 

Web Crawler

  • Crawler run reports now correctly classify empty title and empty body validation errors instead of showing them as "Undetermined" errors.
  • Crawler CSV reports now include error descriptions even when the background worker is terminated due to memory limits.
  • Crawlers now correctly handle all successful HTTP response codes (201-299), not just 200.
  • Removed per-URL ping validation from start URL input to support large-scale crawlers with up to 1500 URLs.

Help Center

  • Fixed product navigation links on custom domains. Admins using custom Help Center domains (for example, help.yourcompany.com) can now correctly navigate to other Zendesk products like Workforce Management from the product navigation tray. Previously, these links pointed to the custom domain instead of the native Zendesk subdomain, causing navigation failures.
  • Updated the "Get help" menu link. The agent navbar's "Get help" menu now points to the correct Knowledge Help Center section instead of the deprecated Support Help Center URL.

Copilot

New:

  • Auto assist can now generate suggestions based on content from external sources and internal knowledge articles. This allows you to broaden the pool of content available to auto assist so it can provide suggestions on even more topics and tickets. See Connecting external knowledge sources to your Zendesk account and Setting up a web crawler.
  • We’re updating the auto assist composer experience in the Agent Workspace to make AI suggestions feel like a natural part of replying to customers - without interrupting an agent’s workflow. Beginning on June 22, we’ll start rolling out this update to accounts over a period of two weeks. See Using auto assist to solve tickets.
  • Auto assist can now use similar solved tickets as a knowledge source across all channels and languages when no procedures or articles are available. This gives agents more relevant reply suggestions based on how customer issues are being resolved in real time, helping teams respond faster and deliver more consistent support. See About auto assist.

AI agents

New:

AI Copilot Procedure Management

  • In the procedure insights side panel, the recommendations section now appears below the insights section for a more logical reading order
  • Article sources in procedure improvement recommendation cards now link directly to the Help Center article instead of the editor. You can review the source content without navigating away from your workflow.
  • When Admin Copilot saves a procedure as a draft, the confirmation message now includes two links - one to open the procedure in the editor and one to return to the full procedures list.

Fixed:

AI Copilot Procedure Management

  • Procedure editor URL no longer carries over pagination state: opening a procedure from a paginated list previously added cursor and pagination query parameters to the editor URL. Those are now dropped on navigation.
  • New procedure recommendations no longer disappear when a malformed ID is present. A single malformed procedure ID in a batch request was causing all new procedure recommendations to be silently dropped for affected accounts. 

App Marketplace

New:
  • FastPass IVM (Support)
    • FastPass IVM is the leading provider of secure identity verification solutions. The FastPass Identity Verification Manager (IVM) for Zendesk brings forced, contextual identity verification directly into the support agent's workflow, ensuring every password reset and sensitive request is handled securely and in compliance with enterprise policy. With this integration, agents no longer need to switch between systems. When a ticket is opened, the app automatically checks ticket status, tags, and requester details against your configured eligibility rules — and either presents a one-click Launch button or automatically opens the FastPass IVM Client. This protects your service desk against social engineering and vishing attacks when they are most likely to occur.
  • ServeTech Skill Tracer (Support) (paid)
    • ServeTech Skill Tracer analyzes your team's real ticket history in Zendesk to identify how each agent performs across ticket categories. It uses a transparent, statistics-based scoring model to surface true specializations and then creates and maintains skill tags in Zendesk automatically — no manual work required. ServeTech works from your existing ticket categories — no custom taxonomy to define, no agents to manually tag. Install it, and your existing Zendesk skills-based routing starts working.
  • ScriptRunner (Support)
    • ScriptRunner helps Zendesk teams automate operational workflows, run secure scripts, and build lightweight internal tools directly inside Zendesk. Use ScriptRunner to handle repetitive admin tasks, validate ticket data, enrich support workflows, and give agents and admins purpose-built tools without switching systems or building a separate Zendesk app for every process.
  • Okta Workflows (Support)
    • Okta Workflows empowers organizations to automate complex identity processes and user lifecycle management without writing code. By integrating Okta Workflows with Zendesk, IT and support teams can seamlessly orchestrate actions based on real-time events. With this integration, you can build custom identity workflows that connect Zendesk to your broader tech stack. Automatically create or update Zendesk user profiles when changes occur in Okta, freeze accounts during offboarding events, or trigger multi-system alerts when high-priority access requests are made.
  • OneClick (Support) (paid)
    • OneClick turns your most common ticket actions into sidebar buttons. Agents update status, assignment, tags, and custom fields in one click—instead of opening multiple fields on every ticket. Save a preset once; apply it to any ticket with a single click. Build buttons in the nav bar app, or share one list account-wide for every agent. Choose who can manage buttons and optionally deploy a shared list via app settings.
  • EVOX (Support)
    • EVOX builds cloud-based call center solutions trusted by customer service teams. This integration connects your EVOX phone system directly to Zendesk Support. Every inbound and outbound call is automatically matched to the right customer and ticket — no manual lookups, no missed records. Instantly identify callers by phone number and open the relevant ticket, automatically create a new ticket and end-user profile when no match is found, and log full call detail records (CDRs) to Zendesk Custom Objects for reporting and compliance.
  • Escalation Guard (Support) (paid)
    • Escalation Guard helps agents submit cleaner, more complete escalations from the Zendesk ticket sidebar. Agents choose an escalation type, complete the required fields, and submit a formatted internal note. Escalation Guard applies routing tags so admins can use Zendesk triggers, views, and automations to route work to the right team.
  • ResolveReady (Support) (paid)
    • ResolveReady helps stop agents from resolving tickets with missing data, skipped steps, or incomplete approvals. ResolveReady enforces ticket completeness before agents can resolve. Admins can build solve-readiness workflows without code. Workflows trigger by ticket tag, form, group, brand, status, or field value. Agents see required steps in the ticket sidebar and complete them once, and each completed item saves directly to a mapped Zendesk ticket field or internal note.
  • VeriDraft (Support)
    • VeriDraft connects to Zendesk and turns any customer message into a ready-to-send reply written entirely from your Terms of Service, SOPs, and compliance documents. Every claim is backed by a real citation, every answer shows how confident it is, and when VeriDraft can't find a grounded answer, it says so — instead of making one up.

Products with no updates this week

  • Admin Center
  • Support
  • AI agents - Advanced
  • Analytics
  • Zendesk Workforce Management (WFM)
  • Zendesk QA

articles.name: Service Incident -  July 9, 2026 - Forethought | Solve widget load failures and elevated API errors
articles.title: Service Incident -  July 9, 2026 - Forethought | Solve widget load failures and elevated API errors
articles.body:
Summary

On July 9, 2026, some customers experienced issues loading the Forethought Solve widget and saw elevated errors when the widget attempted to communicate with our backend services. The issue was caused by a software change that increased backend workload and led to timeouts.
 

Timeline

July 09, 2026 17:34 UTC
We are currently investigating an issue where the Solve Widget is failing to load for some customers. Our engineering team has identified a potential cause and is in the process of rolling back suspected changes to restore service.
 
July 09, 2026 17:41 UTC 
The suspected changes have been successfully rolled back. We are currently seeing traffic recovering and the Solve Widget is beginning to load successfully for affected customers.
 
July 09, 2026 17:58 UTC 
This incident has been fully resolved. The Solve Widget is now loading normally for all customers, and our monitoring confirms that performance and traffic have returned to stable levels following the rollback.
 

Customer impact

Between 16:59 UTC and 17:31 UTC on July 9, 2026, customers using the Solve widget across several pods experienced one or more of the following:
  • The Solve widget failed to open or load
  • The Solve widget displayed frequent error messages
  • Requests to our Solve API returned elevated errors
  • Some customers also experienced degraded access to related dashboards and analytics
During this window, customers could not reliably use the widget.
 

Root Cause Analysis

A recently released change introduced a bug in a synchronization flow used by the widget. Under certain conditions, the widget and backend services retried and repeated work more than intended.
This led to:
  • A spike in “cache misses” (the system could not reuse previously prepared data)
  • Increased fallback to slower backend data retrieval
  • Saturation of backend capacity, causing request queues to build and requests to time out
These effects reinforced each other (retries created more load), resulting in elevated errors and widget load failures.
 

Resolution

We restored service by:
  • Rolling back the problematic release
  • Reducing background load that was competing for the same backend capacity
  • Scaling up the Solve API service to clear backlogs and stabilize performance
After these mitigations, error rates returned to near zero and response times returned to normal.
 

Remediation Items

We’re making changes to prevent similar issues, including:
  • Adding automated tests and safeguards for “non-existent conversation” scenarios
  • Ensuring the widget does not continue polling/retrying in situations where it should stop
  • Adding additional validation before performing expensive backend retrieval work
  • Improving monitoring to detect early signals of this type of overload more quickly
     

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.body:
Question

Can I use an email alias, distribution list, shared mailbox, or Google Group as a support address?

Answer

Zendesk does not support the use of aliases, distribution lists, shared mailboxes, Google Groups, or non-standard email clients or services. These configurations add routing complexities and cause issues with troubleshooting. However, many companies successfully set up and maintain these configurations without issue. Zendesk does not block their use.

To connect these configurations, see To add an external support address in Zendesk.

While aliases, distribution lists, shared mailboxes, and Google Groups are common, they can introduce unique challenges and complications:

  • Complex routing and troubleshooting. Adding another layer of processing increases deliverability risks due to spam filters or lost emails.
  • Malformation of email headers. Relays can alter email headers, which causes Sender Policy Framework (SPF), DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM), or Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC) issues.
  • Fickle nature of email processing. Email behavior can vary based on the processor and parameters, which highlights the need for a direct and simple pathway.
Note: Zendesk highly recommends the use of standard email addresses for maximum deliverability. Unsupported configurations like these can cause issues that an admin cannot troubleshoot. If you use these options, Zendesk cannot help with any problems that arise.

To connect to a Google Group, see How do I use Google Groups as a support address?

articles.name: My Facebook or Instagram integration stopped working
articles.title: My Facebook or Instagram integration stopped working
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

Your Facebook integration, Facebook Messenger, or Instagram Direct channel does not sync or work correctly. You see one of these errors:

  • Messages from Facebook or Instagram do not create tickets
  • Facebook or Instagram users do not receive agent responses
  • You receive an email notification that your Facebook page was deauthorized

    Attention required: Facebook Page, [Name of the page], is no longer authorized
  • You try to reauthorize your Facebook account with Zendesk, but you get an error. The browser shows that the page is linked, but when you return to Zendesk, you see the error below.

    Page not found. The page you're looking for either doesn't exist or you don't have access to it. You cannot reauthorize your Facebook page.

Resolution steps

Important: If you cannot connect your Facebook account to Zendesk for the first time, see Setting up your public Facebook channel.

Zendesk monitors your Facebook pages for new posts, messages, and comments. If Zendesk cannot connect to your Facebook page, it sends an email notification to all admins on your account.

Your Facebook channel can become deauthorized for different reasons:

  • The admin who authorized the Facebook page revoked their Facebook session. This happens when the admin changes their password or signs out of a device after a password change.
  • The admin who added the page removed permissions for the Zendesk Facebook app to manage your pages or access your Facebook page messages.
  • Zendesk receives a consistent response from Facebook indicating that Zendesk is not authorized to access the content of the page. This should only happen due to an error in the platform of Facebook.
  • You have not granted Zendesk management access to your account. For more information, see Setting up your public Facebook channel.

Use the steps below:

Reauthorize the Facebook page again

If you try to reauthorize your Facebook page and see a Page not found message, clear your browser cache and reauthorize the Facebook page again.

Note: Turn on two-factor authentication in your Facebook account if the Meta Business Manager account your Facebook page is linked to requires two-factor authentication. For more information, see Turn on the two-factor authentication requirement in your business portfolio.

To fix this issue:

  1. Sign out of your Zendesk and Facebook accounts

  2. Clear your browser cache and cookies
  3. In the same browser, sign back in to your Facebook account. You must be an admin of the Facebook page.
  4. Sign back in to your Zendesk account as an admin
  5. Reauthorize your Facebook page by following the instructions in Reauthorizing the connection between Zendesk Support and your Facebook pages.

Or watch this video that shows all the steps in the article.

Confirm the Facebook integration works

To confirm the Facebook integration works, follow the instructions in this section Confirming the Zendesk-Facebook connection.

After you reauthorize your Facebook page, the reauthorize required label should no longer appear on the Facebook account.

Next steps if the integration still doesn't work

If you already unlinked your Facebook page from your Zendesk account, remove the Zendesk integration from your Facebook page.

To remove Zendesk from Facebook:

  1. On Facebook, go to the business integrations page to see the list of integrations connected to your Facebook account

  2. Under Zendesk, select Remove to delete this integration from Facebook

To reauthorize Facebook channel pages:

  1. Open a private or incognito window in your browser. Then sign in to both your Zendesk and Facebook accounts
  2. In Admin Center, click Channels in the sidebar, then select Messaging and social > Facebook Pages
  3. Hover over the name of the Facebook page, then click Unlink to remove the page. Repeat this process for all pages you want to unlink
  4. Click Add new page to re-add the Facebook pages you removed in the previous step. For more information, see Reauthorizing the connection between Zendesk Support and your Facebook pages.
  5. Edit the Facebook channel settings for each page and enable Include Wall posts
Note: If you don't select any Facebook pages that have previously been authorized, the Zendesk integration for those pages stops working.

To reauthorize Facebook Messenger and Instagram Direct channels:

  1. Open a private or incognito window in your browser. Then sign in to both your Zendesk and Facebook accounts
  2. In Admin Center, click Channels in the sidebar, then select Messaging and social > Messaging
  3. On the Facebook Messenger and Instagram Direct channels, select the options menu () and click Delete
  4. Select Delete channel in the dialog. Repeat this process for all channels you want to remove.
  5. Click Add channel and select Instagram Direct or Facebook Messenger from the drop-down.
    • For Instagram Direct, click Continue with Instagram to open the Instagram setup flow
    • For Facebook Messenger, click Continue with Facebook to open the Facebook setup flow

See Troubleshooting the Facebook channel

THIS SECTION IS AI CONTENT. DON'T EDIT OR DELETE.

Why does my Facebook integration or Instagram Direct channel fail to sync? What causes a Facebook page deauthorization? Why do Facebook messages not create tickets? Why do customers or visitors not receive agent responses?

Your Facebook or Instagram integration stops working or fails to sync when Zendesk loses authorization. This happens when the agent or support person who authorized the page changes their password, signs out of a device, or removes permissions for the Zendesk Facebook app. Facebook platform errors or a failure to grant Zendesk management access cause this disconnect. When this occurs, messages from customers or end users do not create tickets in your help desk or ticketing system, and visitors do not receive replies from your team.

What permissions do I need to reauthorize a Facebook page? Can I reconnect Facebook if Meta Business Manager requires two-factor authentication? What are the requirements to fix the Facebook integration?

You must hold admin permissions for both your Zendesk ticketing system or help desk and the Facebook page to resolve the connection. Turn on two-factor authentication in your Facebook account if the Meta Business Manager account that links to your Facebook page requires two-factor authentication.

What happens if I do not select a Facebook page that I authorized before during setup? Will my other Facebook pages stop working if I skip them during reauthorization?

The Zendesk integration stops working for Facebook pages that you authorized before but do not select during the setup process.

Does the "reauthorize required" label disappear after I reconnect my Facebook page? How do I know if the Facebook integration works after reauthorization?

Yes. The reauthorize required label no longer appears on the Facebook account after you reauthorize your Facebook page.

How do I reauthorize my Facebook page? How do I fix the "Page not found" error when you link Facebook? What should I do if the browser shows the page is linked but Zendesk shows an error?

If you see a "Page not found" message or error when you try to reauthorize your Facebook page, clear your browser cache and cookies, then use these steps to resolve the issue:

  1. Sign out of your Zendesk and Facebook accounts.
  2. Clear your browser cache and cookies.
  3. In the same browser, sign back in to your Facebook account as an admin of the Facebook page.
  4. Sign back in to your Zendesk help desk or ticketing system as an admin.
  5. Reauthorize your Facebook page.

How do I remove the Zendesk integration from my Facebook page? How do I unlink Zendesk from Facebook business integrations? What are the steps to delete the Zendesk app from Facebook?

If the integration still does not work, remove the Zendesk integration from Facebook using these steps:

  1. On Facebook, go to the business integrations page to see the list of integrations connected to your Facebook account.
  2. Under Zendesk, select Remove to delete this integration from Facebook.

How do I reauthorize Facebook channel pages? How do I unlink and re-add a Facebook page in Zendesk? How to fix Facebook page sync issues in Admin Center?

Follow these steps to unlink and re-add your Facebook pages:

  1. Open a private or incognito window in your browser, then sign in to both your Zendesk and Facebook accounts.
  2. In Admin Center, click Channels in the sidebar, then select Messaging and social Facebook Pages.
  3. Hover over the name of the Facebook page, then click Unlink to remove the page. Repeat this process for all pages you want to unlink.
  4. Click Add new page to re-add the Facebook pages you removed in the previous step.
  5. Edit the Facebook channel settings for each page and enable Include Wall posts.

How do I reauthorize Facebook Messenger and Instagram Direct channels? How do I delete and re-add Instagram Direct or Facebook Messenger in Zendesk? What are the steps to fix Instagram Direct messages that do not sync?

Follow these steps to remove and re-add your Facebook Messenger and Instagram Direct channels:

  1. Open a private or incognito window in your browser, then sign in to both your Zendesk and Facebook accounts.
  2. In Admin Center, click Channels in the sidebar, then select Messaging and social Messaging.
  3. On the Facebook Messenger and Instagram Direct channels, select the options menu and click Delete.
  4. Select Delete channel in the dialog. Repeat this process for all channels you want to remove.
  5. Click Add channel and select Instagram Direct or Facebook Messenger from the drop-down.
  6. For Instagram Direct, click Continue with Instagram to open the Instagram setup flow. For Facebook Messenger, click Continue with Facebook to open the Facebook setup flow.

articles.title: Troubleshooting why reports show null or missing values
articles.body:
In this troubleshooting guide, you will find out what to do if values do not show on a chart in Analytics. At times, you may see 0 or blank values in your report and can investigate the behavior.

This article contains these topics:

  • Verify if the row selector is hidden
  • Check if your columns are hidden
  • Look into your metric filter
  • Verify that you are not hiding part of the result
  • Check that no filter is applied
  • Verify the Top/Bottom filter
  • Compare with actual data

Verify if the row selector is hidden

Verify your Chart configuration settings > have Display Row Selector turned on. The row selector may be hidden and only show selected values.

Check if your columns are hidden

In Result manipulation > Columns, ensure that all columns are visible.

Look into your metric filter

In Result manipulation > verify your Metric filter, perhaps you hid part of the result. For example, in this image, the number in the left should be 0 instead of 20.

Verify that you are not hiding part of the result

In Result manipulation > Hide part of the result, ensure you are not hiding data > Apply.

Check that no filter is applied

At the top of the page and on the left side, ensure that you did not add a filter on your data.

Verify the Top/Bottom filter

In Result manipulation > Check the Top/bottom filter > Untick Top and Bottom > Apply.

Compare with actual data

Finally, if you still see missing values, verify your sources of data. For example, open sample tickets and compare the results with your report.

To learn more about reports, see these articles:

  • Customizing reports
  • Why do I see blank spaces when reporting on articles?
THIS SECTION IS AI CONTENT. DON'T EDIT OR DELETE.

How do I fix empty charts in Explore or reporting? Why does my report show "0" or blank values? How do I troubleshoot "null" or "missing values" in analytics or reporting?

You can investigate the behavior when values do not show on a chart in Explore or analytics or reporting. Use these steps to troubleshoot the report:

  1. Verify if the chart hides the row selector. In Chart configuration settings, turn on Display Row Selector because a hidden row selector only shows selected values.
  2. Check if the report hides your columns. In Result manipulation > Columns, ensure that all columns are visible.
  3. Look into your metric filter. In Result manipulation, verify your Metric filter to ensure you do not hide part of the result.
  4. Verify that you do not hide part of the result. In Result manipulation > Hide part of the result, ensure you do not hide data and select Apply.

If missing values remain, verify your sources of data. Open sample tickets or requests in Support or your help desk or ticketing system and compare the results with your report.
